correctness.rationale: Every edge orientation maps bijectively to two binary rows; the local no-sink conditions give the three-letter alphabet with both special symbols present. Inclusion--exclusion yields all Walsh coefficients. Nonaxial zeros obey a=0 and odd d; axial zero candidates would require 3^a=2^n-1, impossible modulo eight for n>=3. Parity counting gives (3^n-1)/2 zeros. Even support size and an explicit coefficient of magnitude two prove the sharp spectral gap and all stated operator consequences. Boundary n=1,2 is treated explicitly; independent exact-integer computations corroborate through n=8.

value.rationale: The graph family is a canonical tractable subfamily of a generally hard sink-free-orientation counting problem. Its exact Fourier nullity is exponential but exponentially negligible relative to ambient dimension; nevertheless convolution stays singular for all n>=2 and has an n-independent sharp positive spectral gap. This is a natural all-length characterization of operator rank and recoverable-space stability, not just cardinality or an ad hoc finite slice.
